title: Right to Remain Silent
statement: The law talks only about what you say as a witness in court. It does not say that what you tell a social worker is protected.
source_says: Testimony by a parent, guardian, or other person who has the care or custody of the minor ... shall not be admissible as evidence in any other action or proceeding.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Searched 'WIC 355.1 testimony parent not admissible any other action', opened the FindLaw page for 355.1, read subdivision (f). It covers testimony only. The section does not mention statements to a social worker.

title: Right to Remain Silent
statement: If a social worker or the county's lawyer asks you questions outside of court, you can say "I want to talk to my lawyer first." Ask your lawyer how to handle these talks.
source_name: No primary source found (checked Judicial Council booklet, selfhelp.courts.ca.gov, WIC 355.1, rule 5.534)
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Searched for a statute, rule or court guide saying a parent may tell a social worker or county counsel 'I want to talk to my lawyer first'. Opened the Judicial Council booklet Juvenile Dependency Court and You (www4.courts.ca.gov/documents/juvenile-dependency-court-and-you.pdf), selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/juvenile-dependency/guide-parents, the LA DCFS court page and the SF court parent guide. None say it. Only the ACLU SoCal page (aclusocal.org/know-your-rights/california-child-welfare-investigations-101/, not a primary source) says a parent may refuse to answer and ask for a lawyer first. The second sentence (ask your lawyer) matches the booklet p.22 'Keep in touch with your attorney.' Blocked by: no primary source states the first sentence.
fix: If a social worker or the county's lawyer asks you questions outside of court, ask your lawyer how to handle it before you answer.

title: Right to Participate in Case Planning
statement: WIC §16501.1(g)(12): Parents take part in making the case plan whenever possible, and get a chance to read and sign it.
source_says: Whenever possible, parents and legal guardians shall participate in the development of the case plan.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference. Opened the public.law page for WIC 16501.1 and read (g)(12)(A). It also says parents 'shall have an opportunity to review the case plan, and to sign it whenever possible, and then shall receive a copy of the plan.'

title: Right to Participate in Case Planning
statement: Parents have the right to argue for services and placements at disposition (Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(g), right to present evidence at hearings).
source_says: The right to present evidence to the court.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference. Searched 'rule 5.534', opened the courts.ca.gov rule page. Subdivision (g) is 'Advisement of hearing rights' and lists the right to present evidence. The rule covers all hearings. It does not use the words services, placements or disposition, and the entry's parenthetical describes it correctly as the right to present evidence at hearings.

title: Right to Be Heard in Court
statement: If the child lives with you (as a relative caregiver, foster parent, or close family friend), you can tell the judge about the child with the Caregiver Information Form (JV-290) or a letter. If you are a relative but the child does not live with you, use the Relative Information form (JV-285)
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(k)(1)-(2) and (b)
source_says: Written information about the child may be submitted to the court using the Caregiver Information Form (form JV-290) or in the form of a letter to the court.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened rule 5.534. (k)(1) names the current caregiver as 'foster parents, preadoptive parents, relative caregivers, and nonrelative extended family members'. (k)(2) names JV-290 or a letter. (b) says a relative may send information 'using Relative Information (form JV-285) or in a letter to the court.'

title: Right to Be Heard in Court
statement: . You can also ask the judge to let you speak at the hearing.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(b) and Advisory Committee Comment
source_says: judicial officers are encouraged to permit caregivers to orally address the court when caregivers would like to share information about the child.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened rule 5.534. For relatives, (b) says 'On a sufficient showing, the court may permit a relative of the child or youth to: (A) Be present at the hearing; and (B) Address the court.' For caregivers, the Advisory Committee Comment encourages judges to let them speak. Speaking is by the judge's permission, as the entry says.

title: Right to Be Heard in Court
statement: If the child lives with you, you can tell the judge how the child is doing. Use the Caregiver Information Form (JV-290) or a letter, or ask the judge to let you speak.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(k)(2) and Advisory Committee Comment
source_says: The current caregiver has the right to be heard in each proceeding listed in paragraph (1),
steps: SELECT showed the text live in simple_text. Opened rule 5.534 and read (k)(1), (k)(2) and the Advisory Committee Comment. JV-290 or a letter is named in (k)(2). The comment says judges are encouraged to permit caregivers to orally address the court.

title: Right to Your Own Attorney
statement: Your lawyer is expected to meet with you regularly and stay in touch with you.
source_says: Attorneys or their agents are expected to meet regularly with clients, including clients who are children, regardless of the age of the child or the child's ability to communicate verbally
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Searched 'rule 5.660 meet regularly with clients', opened the courts.ca.gov rule page, read (d)(4). It also says 'The attorney for the child must have sufficient contact with the child to establish and maintain an adequate and professional attorney-client relationship.'

title: Right to Privacy
statement: If your placement changes, ask your social worker to make sure all your things move with you.
source_says: ensuring the child has all of their possessions
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Searched 'California foster youth personal belongings move with child placement change', opened the public.law page for WIC 16010.11. The county placement transition policy must cover 'ensuring the child has all of their possessions' and '(D) How the social worker will ensure that the transition plan is carried out as designed.' The entry is advice to ask the social worker and claims no more than that.

title: Right to Participate in Your Case Plan
statement: Ask your social worker to go over the plan with you. If you are 10 or older you have the right to look at it. If you are 12 or older and in a permanent placement, you have the right to a copy.
source_says: A child who is 12 years of age or older and in a permanent placement shall also be given the opportunity to ... receive a copy of the case plan.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened public.law pages for WIC 16001.9 and 16501.1. 16001.9(a)(38) says 'To review the child's own case plan and plan for permanent placement if the child is 10 years of age or older'. 16501.1(g)(13)(A) gives the copy at 12 or older in a permanent placement.

title: Communicate Regularly with the Team
statement: Form JV-290 is due 5 calendar days before the hearing if you hand it in at court, or 7 calendar days before if you mail it (Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(k)(4)).
source_says: for filing no later than five calendar days before the hearing. ... for filing no later than seven calendar days before the hearing.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference. Opened rule 5.534 and read (k)(4). Filing in person is five calendar days before the hearing and filing by mail is seven calendar days before. The Advisory Committee Comment adds that clerks should accept caregiver filings even when they do not strictly meet the deadline.

title: Right to Prepare for Adulthood
statement: If you are 14 or older, your case plan must list the programs and services that will help you get ready for adult life. At 16, you also get your own plan for living on your own (called a TILP).
source_says: For a child who is 14 or 15 years of age, the case plan shall include a written description of the programs and services that will help the child
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened the public.law page for WIC 16501.1 and read (g)(16)(A). (ii) says 'When appropriate, for a child who is 16 years of age or older ... the case plan shall include the transitional independent living plan (TILP)'. Note the statute opens (ii) with 'When appropriate'. Also opened CDSS ACL 08-31 (cdss.ca.gov/lettersnotices/entres/getinfo/acl08/08-31.pdf), which says 'a TILP is to be developed for a youth who is between the ages of 15 1/2 and 16' under MPP 31-236(a).

title: Right to Prepare for Adulthood
statement: Starting at 16, the Independent Living Program (ILP) can help with daily living skills, money, school, jobs, and housing.
source_says: Youth are eligible for ILP services from age 16 to the day before their 21st birthday
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Searched 'CDSS Independent Living Program ILP eligibility age 16', opened the CDSS ILP page. Its service list includes 'Daily living skills', 'Money management', 'Educational Resources', 'Housing (Transitional Housing)' and 'Employment'.

title: Right to Prepare for Adulthood
statement: At 14, your case plan must list help to get you ready for adult life. At 16, you can join the Independent Living Program for help with school, jobs, and housing.
source_says: Youth are eligible for ILP services from age 16 to the day before their 21st birthday
steps: SELECT showed the text live in simple_text. First sentence: opened public.law WIC 16501.1, (g)(16)(A)(i) says 'For a child who is 14 or 15 years of age, the case plan shall include a written description of the programs and services'. Second sentence: opened the CDSS ILP page, which gives age 16 and lists education, employment and housing help.

title: Right to Prepare for Adulthood
statement: Ask about Independent Living Program (ILP) services. ILP starts at 16. Ask your social worker if your county offers anything for younger teens.
source_says: Youth are eligible for ILP services from age 16 to the day before their 21st birthday
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Opened the CDSS ILP page. It gives 16 as the start age and says 'each county has the flexibility to design services to meet a wide range of individual needs and circumstances'. The page does not mention services for younger teens, and the entry only says to ask.

title: Right to Notice of Hearings
statement: You must be told the date, time, and place of each hearing. For the very first hearing, the social worker tells you, and it can be out loud instead of on paper. After that, notice comes in writing and says what the hearing is about.
source_says: The probation officer or social worker shall serve notice as prescribed in this section. ... Service of the notice shall be written or oral.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Searched 'WIC 290.1 initial petition hearing notice social worker orally', opened public.law 290.1: (d)(1) 'The date, time, and place of the hearing.' and (e) written or oral. Opened public.law WIC 291: notice includes '(d)(2) The nature of the hearing.' and '(d)(4) The date, time, and place of the hearing.', served 'by personal service, by first-class mail, or by electronic service' or certified mail. Opened WIC 294: '(e)(4) The nature of the proceedings.' Rule 5.524(h) says 'Notice required by sections 290.1 and 630 may be given orally.'

title: Right to Notice of Hearings
statement: You must be told when and where each hearing is. Notice of the first hearing can be out loud, and later notices come in writing.
source_says: Service of the notice shall be written or oral.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in simple_text. Opened public.law WIC 290.1 (first hearing, written or oral) and WIC 291 (later hearing, 'by personal service, by first-class mail, or by electronic service'). The Judicial Council booklet Juvenile Dependency Court and You p.6 says 'you will be mailed a paper that tells you when and where you need to go.'

title: Right to Reasonable Efforts
statement: The county must make reasonable efforts to keep a child at home. If a child is removed, the county must usually give the parents services to help the family reunify. In some serious cases the judge can decide the county does not have to offer those services.
source_says: Reunification services need not be provided to a parent or guardian described in this subdivision when the court finds, by clear and convincing evidence, any of the following:
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened public.law WIC 361: (e) 'The court shall make a determination as to whether reasonable efforts were made to prevent or to eliminate the need for removal of the minor from their home'. Opened public.law WIC 361.5: (a) 'the juvenile court shall order the social worker to provide child welfare services to the child and the child's mother and statutorily presumed father or guardians.' (b) lists the cases where services need not be given.

title: Right to Reasonable Efforts
statement: When the judge removes a child and at each review hearing, the judge must decide whether the county made reasonable efforts and gave reasonable services.
source_says: the court shall determine by clear and convincing evidence whether reasonable services that were designed to aid the parent or legal guardian ... have been provided or offered
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened public.law WIC 361 (e) for the removal finding on reasonable efforts. Opened public.law WIC 366.21 (e)(8) and (f)(1)(A) for the 6 and 12 month reviews, and WIC 366.22 (a)(3): 'The court shall determine by clear and convincing evidence whether reasonable services have been offered or provided'.

title: Right to Reasonable Efforts
statement: The county usually has to really try to keep your family together, and the judge checks on this at review hearings. In some serious cases the judge can say the county does not have to offer services.
source_says: Reunification services need not be provided to a parent or guardian described in this subdivision when the court finds, by clear and convincing evidence, any of the following:
steps: SELECT showed the text live in simple_text. Opened public.law WIC 361 (e), 361.5 (a) and (b), and 366.21 (e)(8). The duty to give services is the usual rule in 361.5(a), the judge can skip services under 361.5(b), and the judge decides on reasonable services at the review hearings.

title: Right to Be Treated Fairly
statement: You cannot be treated unfairly or harassed because of your race, ethnic group, where your family is from, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or HIV status.
source_says: race, ethnic group identification, ancestry, national origin, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, mental or physical disability, or HIV status.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Searched 'WIC 16001.9 foster youth rights', opened the public.law page (verified Nov. 23, 2026) and read (a)(17): 'to not be subjected to discrimination or harassment on the basis of actual or perceived race ...'. Every item in the entry is on the statute's list. The statute also names gender expression, which the entry leaves out.

title: Speak Up When Something Is Wrong
statement: you have the right to tell someone. Please tell an adult you trust so they can help.
source_says: to contact any or all of these offices immediately upon request regarding violations of rights, ... and to be free from threats or punishment for making complaints.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened the public.law page for WIC 16001.9 and read (a)(41). The offices are the Community Care Licensing Division, the tribal authority, and the State Foster Care Ombudsperson. Telling someone is a right, not a duty, which matches the new wording.

title: Right to Relevant Information
statement: WIC §16010(c) (the agency must give the caregiver the health and education summary); see also WIC §16010.4
source_says: the child protective agency shall provide the caregiver with the child's current health and education summary as described in subdivision (a).
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference. Opened the public.law page for WIC 16010 and read (c): 'As soon as possible, but not later than 30 days after initial placement of a child into foster care', and within 48 hours for each later placement. WIC 16010.4 was not opened in this run. It is cited only as 'see also'.

title: Right to Suggest Relative Placement
statement: Relatives must be checked by the agency. They are looked at first, before foster homes with people the child does not know. Being first in line does not mean the child will always be placed with them.
source_says: "Preferential consideration" means that the relative seeking placement shall be the first placement to be considered and investigated.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened the public.law page for WIC 361.3. (a)(8)(B): 'Those desiring placement shall be assessed according to the factors enumerated in this subdivision.' and 'This inquiry shall not be construed, however, to guarantee that the child will be placed with any person so identified.' (c)(2) defines relative out to the fifth degree with no narrower list.

title: Right to Suggest Relative Placement
statement: Noncustodial parent has right to custody unless detrimental to child (WIC §361.2).
source_says: If that parent requests custody, the court shall place the child with the parent unless it finds that placement with that parent would be detrimental
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference. Opened the public.law page for WIC 361.2 and read (a). It covers a parent 'with whom the child was not residing at the time that the events or conditions arose' and 'who desires to assume custody of the child.'

title: Support the Case Plan
statement: . Follow the visit schedule the judge or social worker sets.
source_says: the capacity to work cooperatively with the agency, birth family, as appropriate, other resource families, and other service providers in implementing the child's case plan
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened public.law WIC 16519.5 and read (c)(1)(C). Opened public.law WIC 362.1: visits come from the court's order, '(a)(1)(A) Visitation shall be as frequent as possible, consistent with the well-being of the child.' Also opened CDSS RFA Written Directives v6.1 (2020), section 11-13(b): care 'in accordance with the case plan of a child or nonminor dependent'. No source uses the words visit schedule or says the social worker sets it. The sentence is advice that fits the duty to help carry out the case plan.

title: Support the Case Plan
source_says: An understanding of the role of the individual or family as a resource family and the capacity to work cooperatively with the agency, birth family, as appropriate
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference. Opened the public.law page for WIC 16519.5 and read (c)(1)(C), which ends 'in implementing the child's case plan and supporting transitions in placement settings or permanency.' It supports the entry's claim that caregivers are expected to support the case plan. It does not mention visits by name.

title: Maintain Sobriety (If Applicable)
statement: The judge may order drug testing as part of your case plan.
source_name: In re Christopher R. (2014) 225 Cal.App.4th 1210, 1214, 1220-1221; WIC 362(d)
source_says: substance abuse treatment and drug testing, parenting classes, individual counseling and monitored visitation.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Searched for the case, opened the copy of the opinion on www4.courts.ca.gov. At p.1214 the parents' court-ordered services included drug testing. At pp.1220-1221 it quotes section 362(d): 'The juvenile court may direct any reasonable orders to the parents or guardians of the child.' Opened public.law WIC 362: the statute itself does not name drug testing. The entry says 'may', which matches.

title: Maintain Sobriety (If Applicable)
statement: A missed test may be counted as a failed test. Ask your lawyer how your court treats a missed test.
source_says: missed one drug test, properly considered the equivalent of a positive test result
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Searched 'missed drug test equivalent of a positive test In re Christopher R.', opened the opinion on www4.courts.ca.gov, p.1217. Also opened the Fresno Superior Court Family Dependency Treatment Court handbook (2013), p.5: 'If you miss a test, it will count as a positive (dirty) test.' The entry says 'may' and tells the parent to ask their lawyer.

title: Maintain Sobriety (If Applicable)
statement: A missed test may count as a failed one, so ask your lawyer how your court treats it.
source_says: missed one drug test, properly considered the equivalent of a positive test result
steps: SELECT showed the text live in simple_text. Same source as the description sentence: opened the opinion on www4.courts.ca.gov and read p.1217. The simple text keeps 'may' and the advice to ask a lawyer.

title: Maintain Sobriety (If Applicable)
statement: If you relapse, tell your lawyer and your treatment provider right away and get back into treatment. Hiding it will make things worse.
source_name: No primary source found (checked Judicial Council booklet, selfhelp.courts.ca.gov, WIC 361.5, two court drug court handbooks)
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. This is advice and states no right, duty or deadline. Opened the Judicial Council booklet Juvenile Dependency Court and You, selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/juvenile-dependency/guide-parents, the SF court parent guide, the Solano Dependency Drug Court policies and the Fresno FDTC handbook. None says what to do after a relapse or that hiding it will make things worse. Fresno p.6 only says 'You must be willing to be completely honest in all communication with the court'. Nothing found contradicts the advice. Blocked by: no source addresses it.
fix: If you relapse, tell your lawyer and your treatment provider right away and get back into treatment. Hiding it can make things worse.

title: Right to Request De Facto Parent Status
statement: This lets you be at hearings, bring a lawyer you hire, and give the judge evidence. The judge may give you a free lawyer but does not have to.
source_says: (1) Be present at the hearing; (2) Be represented by retained counsel or, at the discretion of the court, by appointed counsel; and (3) Present evidence.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened rule 5.534 on courts.ca.gov and read (a), 'The de facto parent may:'. Also opened the Judicial Council guide Caregivers and the Courts, p.10: 'The juvenile court may appoint a lawyer for de facto parents.'

title: Extended Foster Care (After 18)
statement: You do not have to leave foster care at 18. You can stay until 21 if you are in school, working, in a job program, or have a health condition that stops you.
source_says: Nonminor dependents are eligible to receive support until they reach 21 years of age
steps: SELECT showed the text live in simple_text. Opened the public.law page for WIC 11403. (b) 'applies when one or more of the following conditions exist': finishing high school or equal, enrolled in college or vocational school, in a program to promote or remove barriers to employment, 'employed for at least 80 hours per month', or unable due to a medical condition. The simple text says 'working' without the 80 hours. The 80 hours is in the same entry's practical_tips.

title: Extended Foster Care (After 18)
statement: You need to meet at least one condition: in school, in a job program, working at least 80 hours a month, or having a medical condition that stops you from doing these.
source_says: The nonminor is employed for at least 80 hours per month.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Opened the public.law page for WIC 11403 and read (b): 'This subdivision applies when one or more of the following conditions exist:'. (1) and (2) are school, (3) is a program to promote or remove barriers to employment, (4) is 80 hours of work, (5) is 'incapable of doing any of the activities described in paragraphs (1) to (4), inclusive, due to a medical condition'.

title: Be Honest with the Court
statement: If you are not sure how to answer the social worker, ask your lawyer what to do.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet, Juvenile Dependency Court and You, p.22
source_says: Keep in touch with your attorney. Ask questions if there's anything you don't understand!
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Searched for the Judicial Council parent booklet, opened it on www4.courts.ca.gov, read p.22 and p.23 ('You should always talk with your attorney before every court date, anyway.'). The sentence is advice to ask your lawyer and claims no right or rule.

title: Be Honest with the Court
statement: Penal Code §118:
source_says: and willfully states as true any material matter which he or she knows to be false, is guilty of perjury.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference (field reads 'Penal Code §118: Perjury is a criminal offense.'). Searched 'California Penal Code 118 perjury', opened the public.law page, read (a). It covers statements made under oath or under penalty of perjury. It does not cover unsworn talks outside court.

title: Relative Placement Preference
statement: You can still ask if the child is already placed somewhere else. After the disposition hearing, the law says relatives must be looked at first again when the child needs a new placement.
source_says: consideration for placement shall again be given as described in this section to relatives who have not been found to be unsuitable
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened the public.law page for WIC 361.3 and read (d): 'Subsequent to the hearing conducted pursuant to Section 358, whenever a new placement of the child must be made'. The sentence goes on 'and who will fulfill the child's reunification or permanent plan requirements.' The rule is real, but it covers only relatives who have not been found unsuitable and who can meet the child's plan. The entry leaves that out. The first sentence (you can still ask) fits (a): preferential consideration 'shall be given to a request by a relative'.
fix: You can still ask if the child is already placed somewhere else. After the disposition hearing, if the child needs a new placement, the law says relatives must be looked at first again. This is for relatives who were not found unfit and who can meet the child's plan.

title: Relative Placement Preference
statement: Ask about emergency placement. The child may be able to move in after a safety check, before full approval. You then have 5 business days to apply.
source_says: initiate the home environment assessment no later than five business days after the placement.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Searched 'WIC 361.45 emergency placement relative five business days', opened FindLaw 361.45 (current as of January 01, 2026): 'Upon completion of the assessment pursuant to Section 361.4, the child may be placed in the home on an emergency basis.' and the county must require the relative to 'submit an application for approval as a resource family' within the five business days. Opened FindLaw 361.4(a): 'Conduct an in-home inspection to assess the safety of the home', plus a criminal records check and a check of prior abuse allegations.

title: Kin-GAP (Kinship Guardianship Assistance)
statement: . The agreement has to be signed before the guardianship is final.
source_says: The negotiated agreement shall be executed prior to establishment of the guardianship.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Searched 'WIC 11387 kinship guardianship assistance agreement prior to establishment of guardianship', opened the public.law page and read (a). Also opened the CDSS Kin-GAP page (cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/foster-care/kinship-guardianship-assistance): the guardian must have 'entered into a written binding agreement' with the county 'prior to the establishment of the guardianship.' WIC 11364 (state-funded Kin-GAP) requires the agreement but states no timing.

title: Kin-GAP (Kinship Guardianship Assistance)
statement: Tell the worker about all of the child's needs, like therapy or special care. The payment is based on those needs and cannot be more than the foster care rate.
source_says: an amount of aid based on the child's needs and the circumstances of the relative guardian, but that shall not exceed the foster care maintenance payment
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Opened the public.law page for WIC 11364 and read (c). The cap is the payment 'that would have been paid based on the state-approved foster family home care rate' plus 'any applicable specialized care increment'. WIC 11387(c) says the same: 'but that shall not exceed the foster care maintenance payment that would have been paid'.

title: Right to Call the Ombudsperson
statement: They can help with problems about your care, your placement, your services, or your rights.
source_name: WIC 16164(a)(2); fosteryouthhelp.ca.gov File a Complaint page
source_says: Receive complaints made by or on behalf of children placed in foster care, related to their care, placement, or services
steps: SELECT showed the text live in practical_tips. Opened the public.law page for WIC 16164 and read (a)(2). For rights, searched the Ombudsperson site and opened fosteryouthhelp.ca.gov/file-a-complaint/: 'investigating and resolving complaints about foster youth rights, care, placement, and services.' The same page shows the number 1-877-846-1602.

title: Right to Call the Ombudsperson
source_says: and the State Foster Care Ombudsperson, at the time of each placement, and to contact any or all of these offices immediately upon request regarding violations of rights,
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference. Opened public.law WIC 16001.9 (verified Nov. 23, 2026) and read (a)(41), which ends 'and to be free from threats or punishment for making complaints.' Opened public.law WIC 16164: the office receives complaints 'related to their care, placement, or services'. Both sections support the entry (you can call, and you cannot be punished).

title: Right to a Safe and Comfortable Home
statement: Your clothes and your hair and body products should respect your culture. Your food should be healthy and there should be enough of it.
source_says: Clothing and grooming and hygiene products shall respect the child's culture, ethnicity, and gender identity and expression.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in description. Opened the public.law page for WIC 16001.9 and read (a)(3). The first sentence is 'To receive adequate and healthy food, adequate clothing, grooming and hygiene products, and an age-appropriate allowance.'

title: Right to a Safe and Comfortable Home
source_says: To live in a safe, healthy, and comfortable home where they are treated with respect.
steps: SELECT showed the text live in legal_reference. Opened the public.law page for WIC 16001.9 (verified Nov. 23, 2026) and matched each number. (1) safe home. (2) 'To be free from physical, sexual, emotional, or other abuse, corporal punishment, and exploitation.' (3) food, clothing, hygiene products. (17) no 'discrimination or harassment'. (41) contact the Ombudsperson 'free from threats or punishment for making complaints.'
